messages.author: f98fc9da3dc4715b
messages.subject: Colored Plots
parts:
Hey all, I'm looking for some tips on how to make a colored plot for a certain data set I have. I have previously made colored plots and respective legends before with other data sets, but I'm having a bit of trouble trying to execute my previous script with data I've used for a gpagen.

For context, my previous colored plot script was as follows: I converted my excel tables into csv files and read them into R, then used prcomp to do PCA analyses. I then took the scores of the analyses (mydata$x), wrote them to csv files, and read those files into R again, assigning them to objects. I used RColorBrewer package next to make color palette vectors to assign colors to the species I labeled in my files, and also used pch to assign symbols for Male and Female specimens. Finally, I plotted, using the code below.

> plot(PCAnmdScores$PC1, PCAnmdScores$PC2, col=cols_speciesnmd, main="Principal Component Analysis", xlab = "PC1", ylab="PC2")
> legend("topright",legend=paste(c("N_beng","N_cou","N_mena","N_kay","N_pyg","N_java"),times=1),col=cols,pch=1,bty="n",ncol=1,cex=0.7,pt.cex=0.7)

The coloring I want to do this time is to get colored bubbles for my plotTangentSpace results on some landmark digitized data, but since that's proven to be challenging for me so far, and because I know there are other ways to approach one answer, I figured I can somehow extract a set of scores from somewhere in my data (perhaps from my filelist of landmark data in my gpagen or from a PCA analysis on that array). However, the plots I've gotten don't seem to be right. Maybe someone can help direct me to the right set of scores in my data that I'm supposed to be extracting? Or maybe I'm missing a step? Here is a nutshell of a script:

> library(geomorph)
> setwd("~/R/.ply and .nts files")
> Sliders23<-matrix(c(1,15,2,3,16,4,3,17,5,4,18,6,7,19,8,9,20,11,10,21,12,11,22,13,13,23,14),ncol=3,byrow=TRUE)
> all.nts <- list.files(pattern="\\.[Nn][Tt][Ss]$")
> all.data <- readmulti.nts(all.nts)
> gpa.coords <- gpagen(all.data, curves = Sliders23)                         (My all.data filelist of landmark data doesn't seem to have been the answer)
> Links23<-matrix(c(1,15, 15,2, 1,2, 3,16, 16,4, 4,18, 18,6, 5,6, 5,7, 6,8, 7,19, 19,8, 9,10, 9,20, 20,11, 10,21, 21,12, 12,23, 23,14, 14,13, 13,22, 22,11), ncol=2, byrow=T)
> plotAllSpecimens(gpa.coords$coords, links = Links23)
> plotTangentSpace(gpa.coords$coords)            (This is what I am trying to achieve a colored plot for)
> out.pca <- plotTangentSpace(gpa.coords$coords,label = TRUE)                  (Here I used the $scores of my out.pca and wrote them to a csv file, and later even tried a prcomp, but I think I was just totally on the wrong track here with this).

The rest of this script, I'm sure, is pretty much incorrect:

> pcsv <- read.csv("ppc.scores.csv")             (ppc.scores is a renaming of my out.pca, alldatacsv is my all.data filelist)
> cols_pcsv <- cols[pcsv$Species]
> plot(pcsv$PC1, alldatacsv$PC2, col=cols_pcsv, main="Principal Component Analysis", xlab = "PC1", ylab="PC2")
> plot(pcsv$PC1, alldatacsv$PC2, col=cols_pcsv, main="Principal Component Analysis", xlab = "PC1", ylab="PC2")

Any ideas on how to build a code that will help me achieve my desired results?

Thank you!

-Eddie

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Colored Plots
parts:
Hi Eddie,

as you say there are many ways to solve this, but I think the easiest in your case is to grab the PCscores from your plotTangentSpace object, i.e. out.pca$pc.scores and then use the same approach you already used before.

Hope this helps

All the best,

Antigoni

parts:
Hi Antigoni, Thank you for the reply.

I realized that perhaps the reason the plots didn't seem correct to me is because they were 2d plots. By trying to extract the scores of plotTangentSpace, I am essentially extracting scores of a 3d data set in shape space and was only using the x and y axes in my plot code above ($PC1, $PC2), which must have given me a plot that was not including the z axis. Is my intuition correct? This would make much more sense, and I presume that my next step would be to use a code in the plot3d package. If this is the case, which function in that package should I directly go to?

-Eddie

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Colored Plots
parts:
Hi Eddie,

I´m afraid you are not thinking about this the right way. Remember that the physical dimensions of your data do not determine how variation is structured, at least not in the way you are suggesting. Of course for 3D data you have more data dimensions (3*k - 6 after superimposition), but how variation is structured across these dimensions, and what you see in a PCA plot depends on the particular characteristics of your sample, not on the physical dimensions of your landmarks. IN this respect, PCA works exactly the same way for 2D and 3D data, as it would for any kind of multivariate dataset.

I am not sure what you mean by "plots don´t seem correct", what criteria you are using for this judgement or what you are basing your initial intuition on, but PCA plots produced by plotTangentSpace give you the summary of your data. You can look at other PC dimensions (e.g. plot PC2 vs. PC3 or PC1 vs PC3) if you want, but it is not strictly necessary to plot the data in 3D (although you may want to do that to be able to visualize variation in more dimensions, no objection to that). 3D plots in R can be made (not surprisingly!) with the package plot3D.

Hope this helps, good luck with your plotting!
Antigoni
